title: Customer-led deprecation sprint and self-serve migration hub
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: Run a cross-functional, customer-led deprecation sprint that launches a self-serve Migration Hub and associated toolchain to minimize friction when sunsetting API/model variants. This playbook focuses on proactive customer guidance, automated migration tooling, coordinated release notes, and a short assisted runway for high-risk customers.

Goals:
- Provide a single destination (Migration Hub) with step-by-step migration guides, automated compatibility checks, and one-click SDK update suggestions.
- Achieve >= 70% self-serve migrations for non-enterprise customers within the first 8 weeks after public comms.
- Ensure top 50 enterprise customers are either migrated or on a committed plan before enforcement window.
- Reduce post-cutover incidents by >50% via compatibility shims, telemetry, and canary rollouts.

Core deliverables:
1) Migration Hub (Console): migration checklist, endpoint impact matrix, SDK/CLI auto-suggest, sample prompts, rollback instructions, and per-customer status.
2) Migration CLI: local compatibility scanner that flags deprecated fields, incompatible model args, and produces a migration patch suggestion.
3) SDK updates: warning logs for deprecated endpoints, opt-in migrations API, and graceful fallbacks for 30 days after cutover.
4) Release notes and comms kit: in-product banner copy, staged email templates (beta, public, reminder), per-customer comms drafts for Customer Success, and a centralized release notes page with diff highlights.
5) Observability & gating: dashboard for migration adoption, error spikes, latency regressions, and a canary gate that auto-pauses enforcement if error rate > 3x baseline for 30 minutes.

Timeline (high level):
- Week -4 (Kickoff): finalize playbook, legal signoff on comms language, identify top 50 customers.
- Week -3: Engineering implements compatibility scanner and SDK warning hooks; Design ships Migration Hub wireframes.
- Week -2: Beta cohort (20 customers) invited; dry-run internal migration with CS and SEs.
- Week 0: Public announcement + Release notes publish + In-product banner rolled out.
- Week 1-4: Self-serve window + weekly migration progress digest + targeted outreach by CS for top 50.
- Week 5-8: Enforcement warning window: SDK warnings escalate to rate-limited defaults.
- Week 9: Sunset enforcement (final cut) with immediate fallback policies and 48-hour grace for manual rollbacks.

Cross-team responsibilities (summary):
- Engineering: implement runtime gating, compatibility shims, telemetry events, CLI scanner, and SDK warnings. Deliverable: ENG-81212, ENG-81213.
- Design: Migration Hub UX, in-product banners, email templates, localization-ready copy. Deliverable: DES-2204.
- Docs/Developer Advocacy: migration guide, sample prompts, step-by-step snippets for JavaScript/Python/Go.
- Customer Success / Solutions Eng: lead outreach for top customers, build migration playbooks, run migration concierge for the high-touch cohort.
- Sales: enablement deck + FAQ for account teams; list of accounts requiring contract amendments if Reserved capacity impacted.
- Legal/Compliance: review comms, update data-retention notes and audit log language.
- SRE/Oncall: define rollback criteria, runbook for mitigation, and incident comms templates.
- Marketing/PR: coordinate external release notes, blog post, and partner comms once enforcement window is scheduled.

Release notes coordination checklist:
- Single source release notes doc (internal): changes, deprecation timeline, migration links, sample code diffs, risk level per change.
- Generate per-route/api highlights automatically from the deprecation manifest.
- PM to approve final external copy 72 hours before public announcement.
- Provide CS with templated one-pagers for top 50 customers and suggested messaging cadence.

Success metrics and alerts:
- Adoption metrics: percent migrated (self-serve vs assisted), weekly migration velocity.
- Stability metrics: post-cutover error-rate delta, latency P95, % of traffic hitting fallback.
- Engagement metrics: Migration Hub visits, CLI downloads, SDK update installs.
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate >3x baseline for 30m, or >2% of traffic hitting critical errors for 15m.

Acceptance criteria (before enforcement):
- Migration Hub live in Console with at least 3 localized languages.
- Migration CLI passes compatibility test suite and is published to npm/pypi.
- SDKs emit deprecation telemetry and offer programmatic opt-out for testing.
- Top 50 customers have status documented (migrated/planned/blocked).
- Monitoring dashboards for migration adoption and error gating are live.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle multi-variant model families where partial feature parity exists? Proposed: flag partial compat and suggest model-variant mapping.
- Data residency/Private deployments: require separate comms and on-prem migration packages; estimate +4 weeks.
- Enterprise legal: some customers will require contract amendment for reserved capacity changes; Sales needs list by Week -3.

Next immediate steps (this ticket):

- Finalize Migration Hub MVP wireframe with Design by 2025-11-20.
- Kickoff engineering implementation sprint and create scoped ENG subtasks (owner: Eng PM).
